column1: # Measured per-test wall clock for the MAIN integration suite. Used ONLY
# to balance shards (#381, #877).
# A test missing from this file is NOT skipped — it is assigned the mean,
# so the file going stale makes shards less even and never makes one
# incomplete. scripts/test-integration-shard.sh asserts completeness
# independently of this file.
# Provenance (regenerated 2026-08-28, #877). The previous edition was a
# single run from 2026-08-02 and had drifted: 18 of the tree's main-suite
# tests had no row and ran on a mean guess, and 38 rows named tests that
# live in test/integration/harness/ rather than the suite — those rows
# were nearly all 0.00 and dragged the mean that the absent tests were
# costed at DOWN, which is the wrong direction twice over.
#   source     the 22 successful Integration runs that produced suite
#              logs, out of the 24 most recent successful runs in the
#              API's retention window at 2026-08-28T06:00Z (two of the
#              24 were gate-skipped and ran no suite job)
#   method     median of the per-test `--- PASS/SKIP: <name> (<n>s)`
#              lines, across every sampled run. Median rather than mean:
#              the ephemeral runner pool produces occasional slow jobs
#              (job overhead ranged 91-172s over the same window) and one
#              such sample should not move a test's weight.
#   samples    22 for 67 of the 70 tests. The three exceptions are tests
#              that did not exist for the whole window:
#                TestDHCPv6_NoAddressModes_RefuseTheEndpoint         20
#                TestInterfaceName_ProbeSkipPrecedesTheEphemeralFixture  11
#                TestMultiNetwork_SameSubnetRefused                   8
#   corpus     879.2s across 70 tests; mean 12.56s AS SAMPLED. Ten of
#              those rows have since been removed together with the
#              DHCPv6 tests they costed -- see the 2.0 stanza
#              below -- so the table now holds 66 rows, 712.0s, mean
# Runs sampled:
# TEN ROWS WERE REMOVED, AND TWO ARE INFERRED RATHER THAN MEASURED (2.0).
# 2.0 leases through the in-house DHCP library, which speaks
# DHCPv4 only; IPv6 is refused at CreateNetwork until #911. The ten tests
# that drove a v6 client are retired -- named one by one in
# test/integration/ipv6_refused_test.go and in the commit that retired
# them -- so their rows went with them:
#   TestLifecycleMacvlan_IPv6_GoldenPath  TestLifecycleBridge_IPv6_GoldenPath
#   TestTombstoneRestart_PreservesIPv6    TestLeaseRenewIPv6_HonorsT1
#   TestIPv6_DNS6Propagation              TestDUID_PersistsAcrossPluginRestart
#   TestDHCPv6_NoAddressModes_StartTheEndpoint
#   TestDHCPv6_Stateless_ConfigurationReachesTheContainer
#   TestDHCPv6_Managed_StillRequiresALease
#   TestDHCPv6_Managed_ServerSilent_IsStillFatal
# That also retires the #868 stanza this replaces: all four of the rows
# it described were among the ten.
# The two rows that replace them are INFERRED, not measured, and are
# marked here rather than left to look like the rest of the file. This
# branch cannot run the suite -- the integration lane is CI-only -- so
# there is no `--- PASS:` line to take a median of yet. Each figure is
# read off the nearest MEASURED row of the same shape:
#   TestIPv6_RefusedAtCreateWithTheMilestoneNamed  0.10
#     one refused create and one inspect, no fixture and no container.
#     Siblings: TestErrors_NetworkCreateValidation 0.04 (a table of
#     refused creates), TestErrors_ParentIsBridge 0.08.
#   TestIPv6_TheV4PathIsUnaffectedByTheRefusal     5.00
#     one macvlan network that must succeed, no container. Sibling:
#     TestPreflightProbe_PassesOnReachableServer 5.00.
#   TestLeaseRetention_ARestartRebootsRatherThanDiscovers  35.00
#     one container, a full plugin disable/enable recycle and one
#     5s settle. Siblings, added: TestLeaseRetention_NothingEverReleases
#     26.21 (same file, one container, five settles) and
#     TestRecovery_PluginDisableEnable_PreservesEndpoint 7.57 (the
#     recycle alone).
#   TestDNSPropagate_BridgeModeWritesResolvConfToo         8.50
#     added in round 2 for review finding 5(a): bridge-mode
#     propagate_dns was exercised nowhere after the v6 retirement.
#     One bridge network, one container, one resolv.conf poll with a
#     5s ceiling. Siblings, both MEASURED: the macvlan arm of the same
#     assertion, TestDNSPropagate_OptInWritesResolvConf 8.71, and the
#     bridge-mode container tests TestLifecycleBridge_GoldenPath 7.73
#     and TestAddressConflict_BridgeModeDoesNotSelfReport 7.95. Taken
#     just under the macvlan arm rather than at the bridge mean: it is
#     the same test body and the same poll, and the bridge fixture is
#     the cheaper of the two to attach to.
# Refresh all FOUR from the first green Integration run that produces
# suite logs on this branch, by the recipe at the foot of this header.
# FOUR ROWS ADDED AND ONE REWEIGHTED FOR #911, ALL INFERRED, NOT
# MEASURED. The v6 fixture now proves its mode from the wire as well as
# the log, and its contract tests did not exist for any sampled run, so
# there is no `--- PASS:` line to take a median of. Each figure below is
# built from the fixture's OWN measured timings rather than from a
# sibling test, because what dominates these is not the container work
# every sibling shares -- there are no containers here at all -- but two
# waits whose lengths are known:
#   a segment that MUST advertise settles in about 1.0s (dnsmasq's first
#   advertisement, MEASURED 0.950-0.983s over 12 bring-ups, 2026-09-05)
#   plus roughly 1.5s of bridge/iptables/process setup and teardown;
#   a segment that must NOT advertise costs the derived absence window,
#   V6NoRAWindow() = 10s, on top of the same 1.5s.
#   TestV6Fixture_ModesComeUpAsRequested                    21.50
#     was 9.15 MEASURED for four modes. Now five modes, and the no-RA
#     mode spends the derived 10s window where it previously spent a 5s
#     poll that returned early. 4 x 2.5 + 11.5.
#   TestV6Fixture_RefusesASegmentInAnotherModesShape        75.00
#     23 segments: the 25 ordered pairs less the two the signature
#     table cannot separate. Five are named `nora` (one of them the
#     diagonal, which spends the full window; the other four see a
#     forbidden advertisement and stop at once), two spend the 5s
#     positive budget waiting for an advertisement that never comes,
#     and the rest settle in about a second. 11.5 + 4x2.5 + 2x6.5 +
#   TestV6Fixture_AwaitRAAfterAndItsNegative                43.00
#     four live segments, three of them `nora`: 2.5 + 21.5 + 2.5 + 16.5.
#   TestV6RACapture_SeesTheAdvertisementOnTheBridgeAndNotOnAQuietLink
#     one managed segment plus a dummy link; no waits beyond the
#     fixture's own.
#   TestV6Fixture_AssertExchangeRefusesASegmentNoClientEverUsed
#     one managed segment and a one-second budget on a log that cannot
#     change.
# These five are the largest single addition this file has taken and the
# drift matrix alone outweighs any measured row in it, so they are
# flagged for the first refresh rather than left to settle quietly:
# refresh all five from the first green Integration run on this branch,
# by the recipe at the foot of this header.
# FIVE ROWS ADDED FOR THE #725 / #691 PRIVILEGE CELLS, MEASURED AND
# SCALED (sec/privilege-set). Integration run 33927195482, one sample
# each. That run was slow relative to the 22-run medians this file is
# built from, so the raw samples are NOT what is written: they would
# over-weight five tests against every unchanged row, which is the one
# thing this file must not do, since only the RELATIVE weights balance a
# shard.
# The scale factor is derived from the run itself, not assumed. For the
# 58 tests that appear both in this run and in this file with a value at
# or above 1.0s, the median of run/file is 1.4981 (mean 1.4357, p25
# 1.248, p75 1.671). Each new row is its raw sample divided by that
# median:
#                                               raw     written
#   TestSandboxKeyRoute_Macvlan                 12.92      8.62
#   TestSandboxKeyRoute_Bridge                  12.16      8.12
#   TestSandboxKeyRoute_Ipvlan                  12.07      8.06
#   TestSandboxKeyRoute_NonRootContainer        12.03      8.03
#   TestDockerAPI_OnlySafeMethodsReachTheDaemon 12.29      8.20
# The seeded estimates these replace (7.53 / 7.73 / 7.29 / 7.60 / 7.70)
# were sibling-derived and low by 0.4-0.9s, all in the same direction:
# each cell pays for one health read and one `docker exec` that its
# siblings do not.
# TestRecovery_PluginDisableEnable_PreservesEndpoint keeps its 7.57. The
# same scaling puts this run's sample at 7.96, but that row is a real
# 22-run median and a one-sample estimate does not improve it; the cell
# added to that test reads counters already fetched and times nothing.
# FIVE ROWS WERE REMOVED AND SIX ADDED, ALL SIX INFERRED (M6b, conflict_check).
# The chassis's datagram conflict probe is gone; the DHCP library runs
# RFC 5227 in the container's namespace under the per-network
# conflict_check option. The five rows below went with the mechanism
# they costed:
#   TestAddressConflict_SquattedAddressIsReported     5.77
#   TestAddressConflict_CleanSegmentIsNotReported     6.71
#   TestAddressConflict_BareParentIsUndetermined      6.14
#   TestAddressConflict_BridgeModeDoesNotSelfReport   7.95
#   TestConflictProbe_ReclaimsLeftoverRoute          13.73
# The bare-parent case retires outright rather than being ported: a
# Linux host answers an RFC 5227 Probe (sender protocol address 0.0.0.0)
# whatever its routing, so "the parent has no on-subnet address" is no
# longer a reason the check cannot run, and there is no undetermined
# verdict left to assert.
# The six replacements are now MEASURED, from Integration run
# 33909858014 (the first green run of this branch), ONE sample each --
# which the header below says is a worse number than a 22-run median and
# fine, because the value only weights a shard. The inferred figures
# they replace are kept beside them because the difference is the
# interesting part: the arithmetic was an upper bound everywhere, by
# between 0.6s and 10.4s, and the reason is that the RFC windows it
# added are worst cases while the fixture draws the mean.
#                                               measured   was inferred
#   TestConflictCheck_SquattedOfferIsDeclined         36.64      36.00
#   TestConflictCheck_SquatterAfterTheFact            37.61      42.00
#   TestConflictCheck_OffSendsNoProbe                 33.75      37.00
#   TestConflictCheck_WaitAcquisitionIsTimed           9.39      14.00
#   TestConflictCheck_RestartInsideTheAsyncWindow      4.64      15.00  (now 5.98, below)
#   TestConflictCheck_BridgeModeDoesNotSelfReport     11.52      15.00
# The two that moved most say something about the mechanism rather than
# about the estimate. The restart case cost 4.64s at that measurement,
# not 15.0 (it is 5.98 on this branch -- see below): async
# hands the address back before section 2.1 finishes, so the restart
# lands inside the window by construction and the test never waits out
# a probe window at all -- the inferred figure had priced a clean
# acquisition it does not perform. The timed case costs 9.39s against
# 6.71 + 7.0 = 13.71 because 7.0s is section 2.1's WORST window and the
# lane measured 4.92s on the wire, the mean of the entropy draw.
# TestConflictCheck_OffSendsNoProbe is the one that cannot fall much
# further: its 30s quiet window IS the assertion.
# Refresh again from a several-run median once this branch has one.
# THE O-3/O-4 ROWS, NOW MEASURED. Two runs of this branch:
# 33938855928 (five of six jobs green) and 33939820304 (all green).
#                                               measured   was inferred
#   TestHealthDocument_BuildInfoIsWhatTheLaneBuilt     0.01       1.00
#   TestHealthDocument_EndpointEntryMatchesTheContainer 12.43      8.00
#   TestConflictCheck_RestartInsideTheAsyncWindow      5.98       4.64
# The build-identity cell creates nothing at all -- it reads one
# document and one exposition -- so 0.01, not the cheapest measured row
# it was priced at, and both runs agree on it to the sampled precision.
# The endpoint cell is 12.43 from 33939820304, and 33938855928 is NOT a
# second sample of it: the cell FAILED there, and a `--- FAIL:` duration
# is the cost of stopping at the first assertion, which is a lower bound
# on the passing figure and a measurement of nothing. Only the passing
# run is sampled. (The interim 13.00 in this file was that failed run's
# 12.45 plus the assertions it never reached -- inferred, and marked so
# while it stood.)
# The restart case is the M6b (d) refresh and the only row here with two
# samples: 6.24 and 5.71, so 5.98. Both are above the 4.64 this replaces
# and the 4.64 was itself measured, so the rise is a real change, not
# noise: this branch anchors the probe window on `backAt` rather than
# `ackAt`, which is later, so the case now spans the plugin coming back
# rather than the ACK before it. The (d) refresh and the (c) fix are the
# same edit. The spread between the two samples (0.53s) is the scale of
# what a single sample buys anywhere in this file -- the rows above were
# medians of 22.
# ONE ROW IS A SKIP COST, NOT A RUN COST.
# TestInterfaceName_MultiNetworkDeterministic skipped in all 22 samples —
# the engine does not yet honour a plugin-returned DstName (#125), so the
# test's probe runs a throwaway container and then skips. Its 7.41s is
# therefore the cost of the PROBE. When the engine ships that support the
# test activates and this row becomes an underestimate; refresh then.
# THIS FILE IS THE MAIN SUITE ONLY. TestFailure_* runs in its own
# unsharded job and TestMain is not selectable, so neither is costed
# here. scripts/check-durations-table.sh enforces the set both ways: a
# main-suite test with no row is an error, and a row naming anything the
# partitioner will not place is an error too — a stray row is what
# poisoned the mean above.
# To refresh, from green runs (aggregate several, do not trust one):
#   gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/actions/runs/<id>/logs > run.zip
#   unzip -p run.zip '*_main-*-suite.txt' \
#   # then take the median per test across runs, and re-run
#   # scripts/check-durations-table.sh
# A TEST WITH NO CI HISTORY has no line for that recipe to harvest: it
# reads green runs, and a test added on a branch has never been in one.
# check-durations-table.sh reddens on the missing row all the same, so
# the recipe needs a second half or every new main-suite test costs its
# author a round (#878). Measure it once yourself and add the row:
#   # same preconditions as `make integration-test` (root, plugin built
#   # and installed); ONE test, not the suite
#   go test -v -tags integration -count=1 -timeout 20m \
#     -run '^TestYourNewTest$' ./test/integration/...
#   # take the `--- PASS: <name> (<n>s)` figure, add the row, then
#   # scripts/check-durations-table.sh
# One sample is a worse number than a 22-run median and that is fine:
# the value only weights a shard, and the next regeneration replaces it.
# No row is the strictly worse option — it costs the test at the mean
# AND reddens the gate.
